newsitem.title: USA: Dominican government says no death penalty.
newsitem.headline: Dominican government says no death penalty.

text.p: The Dominican Republic has conditioned the return of the first two nationals extradited here in several decades on the United States not seeking the death penalty, a federal prosecutor said on Thursday.
The two men, Francisco Medina, 30, and Maximo Reyes, 37, arrived in New York on Wednesday to face separate indictments charging them with violent murders and drug trafficking.

"We had anticipated that the Dominican Republic would condition the extradition of these defendants on the United States not seeking the death penalty," said Mary Jo White, U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York. "The U.S. government has just received a fax of the presidential decree and it does contain such a condition."
She said, however, that a formal decision not to seek the death penalty cannot be made until the decree is reviewed by Attorney General Janet Reno.
White's statement was released several hours after a court hearing in which a prosecutor in her office said that the government was considering seeking the death penalty in one of the cases.
The comment was made during the arraignment of Medina, who is known by several aliases, including "Freddy Krueger" after the villain in a series of horror movies.

Medina, who was arrested by Dominican police in April, is charged in a lengthy indictment accusing him of drug trafficking and more than a dozen violent murders in New York. Authorities allege he was an enforcer for a vicious drug gang called the Wild Cowboys involved in the distribution of crack cocaine and heroin in Manhattan and the Bronx.
Reyes, who was arrested in May, is accused of being a co-leader of another violent drug group called the Company that operates in Brooklyn.
The United States has had an extradition treaty with the Dominican Republic since 1910, but a law passed by the Dominican legislature in 1969 barred the extradition of Dominican nationals.

Labe Richman, who was appointed by the court on Thursday to represent Medina, said he would investigate Medina's claim that his arrest was illegal because of the 1969 law and that his seizure amounted to kidnapping.
Medina and Reyes are being held in a Manhattan federal prison and a bail hearing has been set for Wednesday.
